DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (Pseudotumor Cerebri).

The clinical picture of a 69-year-old woman with a 3-week history of worsening headache and progressive vision loss, without systemic symptoms like fever or weight loss, strongly suggests increased intracranial pressure. I have already ruled out infectious and obvious traumatic causes through your history; the absence of morning headaches or nausea makes a tumor slightly less likely but does not rule it out. However, given the classic presentation of papilledema causing visual decline, the most probable diagnosis is Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension. To confirm this, I would typically request a lumbar puncture to measure opening pressure, but based on the current evidence and the urgency of preserving vision, I am confident in this diagnosis.
